title: Service-worker auto-update reloads the page mid-edit and destroys unsaved new-note content (create draft never persisted)
description: When a new service worker deploys, registerType:"autoUpdate" in vite.config.ts makes the bundled registerSW force an unconditional window.location.reload() on all open clients. The Create-note form contains an uncontrolled textarea (<textarea name="content"> at line 194) with no onChange handler or persisted state, so composing a new note loses all typed content when the page reloads mid-edit. createDraftKey() exists in writeDrafts.ts (lines 12-14) but is imported nowhere and never used by the create path, unlike the Edit path which persists draftContent to localStorage on every keystroke.
why: The Create-note textarea stores content only in the DOM with no localStorage persistence, so an auto-update reload destroys it with no recovery mechanism. Affects every client because autoUpdate reloads unconditionally.
fixSketch: Persist the create-dialog textarea to localStorage under createDraftKey() on input (debounced), restore it when the dialog opens, and clear it on successful note creation. Alternatively make the dialog controlled and lift content into App state. Independently, gate the auto-reload listener so it does not fire while an edit or create form is dirty.
provenance: transcribed from 01-service-worker-pwa.md (Opus finder confirmed; no adversarial-panel state file existed)

title: No periodic SW update check — iOS standalone PWA can run stale cached JS against a newer backend for an entire session
description: registerSW is called with only immediate:true and onNeedRefresh; no periodic registration.update() interval is configured. On iOS WebKit standalone PWAs that are backgrounded and resumed, the browser does not re-fetch the service worker script, so no update check fires and the old precached JS/CSS bundle persists indefinitely while the backend API has moved forward, risking frontend/backend contract drift.
why: Engine-specific to WebKit/iOS standalone: Chrome and Firefox re-check the SW on each navigation, but iOS standalone PWAs commonly suspend without triggering a navigation, so without an app-driven periodic update() call the old precache persists much longer than expected.
fixSketch: Add an onRegisteredSW(swUrl, r) callback that calls r && setInterval(() => r.update(), 60*60*1000) and also triggers r.update() on visibilitychange/focus events, so long-lived iOS PWA sessions pick up new deploys without manual relaunch.

title: Installable PWA has no API runtime caching — offline yields a working shell but every note/tree request fails
description: The workbox config sets only globPatterns (app shell precache) and navigateFallbackDenylist; there is no runtimeCaching entry for /api routes. The manifest declares display:standalone and a full icon set, so the app is installable and presents as offline-capable, but offline the precached shell loads while all API requests fail, yielding an empty app rather than true offline content reading.
why: All install-capable engines cache and serve the shell while offline because index.html is precached, but none can return /api data since nothing caches it. This mismatch between the install affordance and offline capability creates a degraded experience.
fixSketch: Either add a NetworkFirst/StaleWhileRevalidate runtimeCaching rule for read-only GET /api/note and /api/tree so recently viewed content survives offline, or reset expectations by not promoting install or explicitly showing an offline-unavailable state.

title: onNeedRefresh in main.tsx is dead code under autoUpdate — there is no hook to flush drafts before the forced reload
description: The onNeedRefresh callback is unreachable under autoUpdate mode.
why: REFUTED: the reload still occurs correctly via the library's activated listener; the dead code is a code-quality issue, not a behavioral defect on any named client.
